body:
Independent READ-ONLY exact-SHA review of 72e6832 against parent 75fd2a3. ACCEPT; I did not rerun the reported full gate.

MassRatio.of now judges both subset constraints in dimensionless quotient space. The tiny-scale pin MassRatio.of(0.0, 1e-9, 1e-12).isLeft is the decisive regression against the old absolute epsilon. Accepted overflow is absorbed in dependency order: conditioning is clamped to total, then numerator is checked/clamped against that normalized conditioning, so stored conditioning <= total, numerator <= conditioning, value <= 1, and support <= 1 exactly. Zero-whole handling still distinguishes 0/0 (lawful absence) from positive mass over zero (typed refusal); non-finite/negative gates precede division. Clamping, rather than proportional scaling, preserves the subset semantics.

ExternalMassReport's whole is dimensionless 1.0, so the absolute 1e-9 there is already a quotient tolerance. When the admitted pair exceeds 1 only within tolerance, proportional normalization preserves its split and the complement construction pins the stored sum exactly to 1; under-1 pairs remain under-1, so the type does not invent partition completeness. The 1e-9/2e-9 pins and raw-store mutations exercise both capacity and refusal.

The tested base divergence is governance-only 411e359 (AGENTS.md); no compiled/test source differs. No findings.
